newsitem.title: USA: Northeast names Morris CEO, chairman.
newsitem.headline: Northeast names Morris CEO, chairman.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Tuesday it named Michael Morris president, chairman and chief executive officer, effective immediately.
Formerly with Michigan's largest utility, Morris, 50, replaces Bernard Fox, who announced his retirement earlier this year.
Morris told reporters in a teleconference that he was confident Northeast could solve its current nuclear and regulatory problems in Connecticut and New Hampshire.
"We can work our way out of this situation," Morris said. "We truly believe it is solveable."
Northeast's three Millstone nuclear plants in Waterford, Conn., have been closed for safety reasons since March 1996.
"What we clearly need is a single point of leadership, so that we can help the team accomplish the goals they need," Morris said.
"If our nuclear program progresses as we believe it will, it will take us into a much brighter day."
Northeast has said it expects to have all three Millstone units ready for restart by early 1998.
The utility has projected its nuclear outage-related costs at $990 million through 1998.
Morris said his contract was for five years, but he declined to disclose his salary.
Asked why he would want the job as leader of the beleagured utility, Morris said: "That's an interesting question."
"I really believe that Northeast Utilities has tremendous foundational strengths."
He said that, not too long ago, the company "was held forth as one of the models in the electric utility business."
"I guess I'm young enough, and energetic enough, to believe that, building off of those strengths, we can re-establish NU at that place," Morris said.
"I enjoyed the challenges that I've gone through before, and I see many of them (as) very similar here."
Morris was formerly with CMS Energy Corp in Dearborn, Mich., where he served as president and chief executive officer of CMS subsidiary Consumers Energy, an electric and gas utility.
He said he was closely involved in helping restructure Michigan's electric industry over the last three years.
Consumers Energy, Michigan's biggest utility, operates a number of fossil and hydro electric generating plants and two nuclear stations, for which Morris oversaw operations.

Northeast's board of trustees liked Morris because "he has operated successfully in both the regulated and deregulated business environments," said Elizabeth Kennan, lead director of the Northeast board of trustees.

"It's clear that we have a very serious challenge here," Morris said. "But having seen other plants go through the same process... these issues are solveable." Northeast stock closed up 0-01 at 9-11 on Tuesday.
((--Matthew Lewis, Hartford newsroom, (860) 727-0224))
